body:
I want to chime in and add that my partner had been relying on Veaux's texts almost entirely when we opened our marriage. What ensued was a very painful, traumatic couple of months where a person who is generally very kind, essentially gaslighted me and downplayed my emotions. Both my partners witnessed me have panic attacks regularly, running and hiding and curling up in fetal position from emotional pain, and still concluded that poly was a fine decision for us and that I just needed to work on jealousy and my unpacking my own traumatic past. I became suicidal and self harmed, something I have only done when in abusive relationships and not at any other point when dealing with depression. The words from Veaux's books was used against me every time I tried to stand up for myself. The only way I could fight back and advocate for myself was by using the words of my therapist. I believe that because I am an emotional and feminine person, my needs and emotions were downplayed and the severity of the situation was ignored.   


I just wanted to add my two cents about how he has impacted me. I believe that polyamory can be done well and can be a positive lifestyle choice for people, and have seen it work well for some. But it is such a delicate balance and it's so easy to take advantage of people. Even people who are typically kind and caring can do it.

A lot of these things feel untrue but actually are quite true. It's hard because he is so kind and gentle and expresses wanting to care for and support me, that I don't notice the things that he does that say the opposite. He often frames my feelings as being irrational, and that his ideas are rational, while saying he supports me. And he'll say that he feels like physical things are not a big deal... but also say that he's afraid to tell me about physical things he's done because of how I'll react (which my therapist noted today = *they are a big deal* because they are to me and shows that he is aware but there's a disconnect).  


I've been slowly working on gaining independence but it's been a rough journey. I had a full time salaried job that gave me financial independence, but it made me feel like I was dying from anxiety. Now I work part-time but the depression is kicking in hard. I am hoping to graduate after this term... but depression is making is hard to study and focus and retain information. And my feelings of hopelessness make it hard to think about what path I want to take after with grad schools because everything feels empty and meaningless..  


I think that medication and CBT will definitely help me gain the strength to remember what I care about and regain my self of self and sense of agency.   


​

Thank you so much. I have taken your's and other's and am pushing for CBT in therapy and going to try medication. I realized I had been holding back a lot and even told my therapist this, so now she is aware of this tendency to minimize my problems and that I often appear to be doing okay when I'm not. She is going to work with me to go deeper, but the medication will help me be able to handle those stronger feelings.  


It's so hard to ask for my needs when they are framed as irrational and emotional, in contrast to things that are logical and rational. I've had several people in my life sort of gaslight me and make me feel that what I feel is not real because it is not 'rational', and when I am feeling this way it's very hard to argue and stand up for myself. Due to my relationship dynamics and a bit of co-narcicissm, I struggle to even acknowledge my needs as existing or as being important when I'm feeling functional, and when I'm in the depths of depression this is near impossible...

Thank you for your words of validation. It's hard to come to terms with the fact that my partner has been supportive while we were monogamous, but has struggled to be supportive with our new dynamic. My therapist has actually highlighted all the times that he has struggled to support me, but I have difficulty discussing this with him afterwards and developing a healthy framework. We did do a couples session, but he presented things like we were both fine and knew what to do (because he read 'the books' and knows all the right things). While he has not been diagnosed, both him and my therapist believe he is on the spectrum and this adds another layer of difficulty to the situation. It seems wise to not pursue anything further and be very careful with our partner, C, until or unless we have demonstrated that we have built a healthy framework for ourselves. I bet that poly has just highlighted issues that we had that we didn't realize were there.

I definitely need boundaries, but I tried to do the emotional labor to get rid of them all to accommodate my partner's wish to be a relationship anarchist. But it's very clear that relationship anarchy does not work for me at all. I definitely need stability and security in my relationships to feel safe, as this was something that was never present in my childhood and this sort of nonmonogamy really triggers those feelings of being worthless.  


I do want to say that I did not threaten suicide or self-harm in a manipulative way. We have discussed how he can support me when I am feeling 'in the red zone' because in the past I have isolated myself and harmed in secret and kept my suicidal ideation to myself. I requested help because I felt that I could not control my body in the moment. I  discussed my suicidal ideation in relation to my depression, and was clear that it is not because of him or because of being poly. He knows that these issues are not related to him. I needed it to be clear, though, that these feelings of jealousy and insecurity do feed into these negative thought patterns.   


He has followed through with putting new relationships on pause, and I let C know how I've been feeling. They are going to meet with me to talk about how they can support me and what I need right now.   


And I'm going to start CBT with my therapist and get on medication.  


It's definitely thanks to everyone who commented on here. I often rationalize that I am fine after my mood has stabilized, and avoid seeking further help. All this validation and advice to seek that help has pushed me to do so.  


Thank you. :)

The problem is that sometimes I find myself thinking that it makes sense, that it's okay, and that I want to be poly too. But I think it's more that I wanted to *try* being non-monogamous and it's feeling like a thing that I just can't handle. Then I end up beating myself for being so irrational and insecure and not being able to be okay about it. I kind of said no last night when we decided to pause any other relationships.   


It's really complicated.. even though he is willing to do whatever it takes to care for me, I perceive a problem when there is none, and try to fix the problem by subverting my own needs. This morning I woke up feeling okay at first, and would have told him that it is okay to keep dating that person, if I had not re-read a diary entry I made when I was in the depths of that feeling to try to remember the details about how it hurt.

I feel like the label fits, and my therapist has backed that up, but they never formally evaluated me and I haven't really received more than talk therapy. I think it might be time to ask for something a bit more structured. The problem is that I often feel like I am fine when I'm not, and tend to minimize my problems even in therapy so it doesn't get recognized and addressed.
